summary.headline: Zydus Wellness Q2 FY27 consolidated net sales rose 74.6% YoY to INR 11,227 million, with EBITDA up 271.7% to INR 855 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 net sales were INR 11,227 million (+74.6% YoY) and H1 net sales were INR 25,526 million (+70.1%), with the Comfort Click acquisition inflating the inorganic growth. Domestic portfolio grew 29.2% in the quarter but only 13.3% in H1, as seasonal brands rebounded from a weak Q1. International like-to-like growth slowed to 12.4% in Q2 from 18.6% in H1, with management attributing the slowdown to a Prime Day shift, a website migration in one market and softer Amazon sales in one or two markets. Management said gross margin improved in the core business on a like-for-like basis, while sequential gross margin may look lower due to seasonal mix, and it took calibrated price increases of under 2% blended.

segments.name: Domestic portfolio
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 29.2% with seasonal brands +123.5% on low base; H1 growth 13.3% with seasonal brands -8.7%. Management said rural demand is holding and growing slightly faster than urban.

segments.name: Skin and hair care
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 37.5%, H1 35.8%; Everyuth grew at double-digit rates, Cuticolor saw strong uptake with Bright Brown launch. Management says Everyuth facial cleansing share rose from rank 7 to rank 4 in a category of about INR 4,500 crore.

segments.name: Food and Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q2 growth 25.1%, H1 20.7%. Complan posted double-digit growth for a third straight quarter; Nutralite grew strong double digits; Sugar Free grew double digits; RiteBite Max Protein sustained strong growth.

segments.name: International (Comfort Click)
segments.commentary: Like-to-like growth 12.4% in Q2 and 18.6% in H1, versus 25% growth reported last quarter per analyst. Management targets double-digit growth for H2 and states Comfort Click EBITDA margin steady state of 14-15%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit growth for Comfort Click to continue into H2 FY27, though Q2 was below its internal expectation.
Core business EBITDA margin to improve through gross margin gains and operating leverage; management says it is confident of medium-term margin expansion despite inflation.
Management intends to match or improve domestic gross margins in H2 FY27 despite the high base in H2 FY26, but said outcome is uncertain in a volatile environment.
Further calibrated price increases planned in H2, targeted at specific SKUs where commodity costs (e.g., milk, PET) rise; palm oil has stabilised.
Domestic A&P to stay at about 12.5%-13% of sales; Comfort Click A&P at 23%-24%, with stepped-up middle and top funnel spend.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Newly set up own medical marketing team supports direct supply for Complan NutriGro (2-6 year toddler range).
RiteBite Max Protein cookies (10 g protein, no palm oil, maida or added sugar) launched pan-India across online and offline channels.
demand_pricing: Blended price increase taken so far is less than 2%, applied only to SKUs with direct input cost impact; commodity inflation in single digits, with dextrose under annual tie-up.
Comfort Click slowdown attributed to Prime Day timing shift from June to July, a website migration in one market, and softer Amazon sales in one or two markets; management called these temporary.
Newer launches contributed about 2% of growth in the last year, with launches over 3-4 years at about 4% (per management's reply to a question).
Competitive intensity in Comfort Click is higher than expected, which management said was anticipated, and more players are entering functional snacking (RiteBite).
Complan growth attributed to celebrity campaign, 50% lower sugar relaunch and NutriGro relaunch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Comfort Click growth slow from 25% to 12%, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a Prime Day shift from June to July, a website migration in one market and marketplace slowdowns; H1 international growth is 18%+ and double-digit growth is still targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Is Amazon slowing for Comfort Click?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two markets saw Amazon slowdown that it considers temporary; it is expanding to Boots and other marketplaces.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state A&P?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic A&P stays at about 12.5%-13% of sales; Comfort Click A&P runs at 23%-24%, and management will not cut marketing to expand EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What are Comfort Click margins and the price increases taken in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Comfort Click EBITDA margin steady state is 14-15%; management would not give brand-level margins and said price increases were calibrated and not portfolio-wide.

qa_highlights.question: Can consolidated gross margin return to the 65% range if Comfort Click growth recovers to 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it hypothetical, said the company would be in a similar zone, and said it would revert with a calculation.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Comfort Click margin pressured like-for-like given strong domestic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Comfort Click margins are holding well and that it invested in domestic brand building, which weighed on the bottom line.

risks_watch: Comfort Click growth decelerated to 12% in Q2 from 25% last quarter; H2 double-digit target depends on recovery in marketplace and website-shift markets.
Heightened competition in Comfort Click and new entrants in functional snacking (RiteBite) could pressure growth and pricing.
Commodity inflation (milk, PET, palm oil) may require further price increases and could dent consumer demand if sustained.
Sequential gross margin may look lower in Q3 due to seasonal mix; H2 faces a high base from last year's strong gross margins.
Seasonal brands (Glucon-D, Nycil) remain negative in H1 at -8.7%, and management does not disclose seasonal brand contribution.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core domestic business and Complan/Everyuth momentum, but cautious and evasive on Comfort Click margins, quarter-specific price increases and brand-level numbers, which management repeatedly declined to share.
key_quotes: So, all I can tell you is that I think margins, Comfort Click is holding rather well.
We have a pricing power across our brand portfolio, and we'll pass on these.
So, in short to medium term, I think we'll remain consistent about 12% to 13%, 0.5% any time we have an opportunity, we'll take out, but not a significant shift.
We do believe that we will stay on course to get to a double digit for half year 2 as well.

growth.why: Management guides double-digit Comfort Click growth into H2 FY27 and core gross margin/EBITDA improvement, backed by brand momentum (Everyuth share gains, Complan growth, RiteBite launch) and calibrated pricing, but no capacity additions, capex or orders were discussed and utilisation was not stated.
